resources.string: Say “hey %1$s” or just “%1$s” and the assistant opens by itself, hands-free. It compares your voice with 4 recordings of you, so it works with any name and language, even an invented one.
Off by default. Keeps listening with the screen off.
Paused: another app is using the microphone
Stopped: the system turned it off or the phone restarted
Uses battery: the microphone stays on while this is active.
Shows a persistent notification and Android shows the microphone indicator (green dot) the whole time.

Privacy: “%1$s” is detected inside your phone and audio does not leave it until it hears you. Only then is your command recorded and sent to Whisper (Groq) as usual. Your recordings are deleted; only numeric fingerprints are kept.
Without the “Display over other apps” permission I can’t open the assistant by myself: I’ll show a notification you have to tap.
For the assistant to open by itself when you say “%1$s”, Android requires the “Display over other apps” permission. Without it, it works through a notification you have to tap.
“%1$s” is very short and may trigger by accident. It works, but a common 2–3 syllable name works better (optional).
“%1$s” has a single syllable and may fail more. A common, short, 2–3 syllable name works better (optional).
“%1$s” is long or hard to say and may fail. A common, short, 2–3 syllable name works better (optional).
“%1$s” has numbers or symbols. Say it as you pronounce it; a simple name is still better.
You changed the AI’s name: record “hey %1$s” and “%1$s” again to turn listening on.
Your recordings were deleted and listening was turned off
Turn on the voice assistant first (above)
Almost never triggers by mistake, but may sometimes miss you.
Hears you more easily, but may trigger on other voices or noises.
Without always listening, the assistant opens with the power button or the tile, and inside you can also start by saying “hey %1$s” or “%1$s”.
Audio is analyzed on your phone and does not leave it until it hears you.
Android stopped it. Tap to turn it back on.
The phone restarted or the app was updated. Tap to turn it back on.
I couldn’t keep listening. Tap to turn it back on.
I couldn’t turn listening back on. Enable it from Settings > AI.
Now say just “%1$s” (without “hey”) in your normal voice.
First say “hey %1$s” in your normal voice.
Do it somewhere quiet, about 30 cm from the phone. It doesn’t have to sound identical every time.
I didn’t hear you. Try again.
That was too short. Say the full phrase.
Done: your voice was saved as numeric fingerprints (the audio was deleted).
Your recordings are quite different from each other and it may fail more. To improve it, record again somewhere quiet.
I couldn’t prepare the detector. Reinstall the app or report the error.
I couldn’t use the microphone (is another app using it?)
We’ll run two short tests: first you say the phrase several times, then you talk normally to check it doesn’t trigger by mistake.
Say it about 5 times, pausing 2 seconds between each. Only the phrase.
Chat, read aloud or play music or TV, without saying the phrase. False activations are counted (10 s).
Detected %1$d of %2$d times (%3$d%%) and triggered %4$d times by mistake.
Low detection. Try re-recording where you usually use it, raising the sensitivity or choosing a more distinctive 2–3 syllable name (AI name, above).
It triggers too often. Try lowering the sensitivity, re-recording more clearly or choosing a name less similar to common words.
I didn’t hear you during the test. Check the microphone permission and that no other app is using it.
